## Overview

This module handles creating new "block" configuration files for Continue (a dev tool), supporting several block types.

## Block type mapping

`BLOCK_TYPE_CONFIG` maps each `BlockType` to a `singular` label and a `filename` base:

| Block type | singular | filename |
|---|---|---|
| context | context | context |
| models | model | model |
| rules | rule | rule |
| docs | doc | doc |
| prompts | prompt | prompt |
| mcpServers | MCP server | mcp-server |
| data | data | data |

## File extensions

`getFileExtension` returns `"md"` for `rules` and `prompts`, otherwise `"yaml"`.

## Key functions

- **`getContentsForNewBlock(blockType)`** — Builds a `ConfigYaml` object with `name`, `version: "0.0.1"`, and `schema: "v1"`, then adds type-specific defaults (e.g., a `file` context provider; an Anthropic model with roles `["chat", "edit"]`; a default rule string; docs pointing at the Continue docs; a unit-test prompt; or an `npx`-based MCP server config).

- **`getFileContent(blockType)`** — For `rules` uses `createRuleMarkdown`, for `prompts` uses `createPromptMarkdown` (with `invokable: true`), otherwise serializes the config object via `YAML.stringify`.

- **`findAvailableFilename(...)`** — Determines the extension, computes a base filename (sanitizing rule names, defaulting to `"global-rule"` for global rules or `new-<filename>` otherwise), then loops appending a numeric suffix until it finds a non-existing file URI.

- **`createNewWorkspaceBlockFile(...)`** — Validates that workspace dirs exist, builds a base dir under `.continue/<blockType>`, finds an available filename, writes the content, and opens the file.

- **`createNewGlobalRuleFile(...)`** — Creates a rule file under the global Continue path's `rules` subdirectory (with `isGlobal = true`).

+/**
+ * Parses markdown content with YAML frontmatter
+ */
+export function parseMarkdownRule(content) {
+    // Normalize line endings to \n
+    const normalizedContent = content.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
+    // More reliable frontmatter detection
+    const parts = normalizedContent.split(/^---\s*$/m);
+    // If we have at least 3 parts (before ---, frontmatter, after ---), we have frontmatter
+    if (parts.length >= 3) {
+        const frontmatterStr = parts[1];
+        // Join the remaining parts back together (in case there are more --- in the markdown)
+        const markdownContent = parts.slice(2).join("---");
+        try {
+            // Parse YAML frontmatter
+            const frontmatter = YAML.parse(frontmatterStr) || {}; // Handle empty frontmatter
+            return { frontmatter, markdown: markdownContent.trim() };
+        }
+        catch (e) {
+            // Error parsing frontmatter, treat as markdown only
+            console.warn("Error parsing markdown frontmatter:", e);
+            return { frontmatter: {}, markdown: normalizedContent };
+        }
+    }
+    // No frontmatter found
+    return { frontmatter: {}, markdown: normalizedContent };
+}

+ * Converts a markdown file with YAML frontmatter to a RuleWithSource object
+ */
+export function convertMarkdownRuleToContinueRule(path, content) {
+    const { frontmatter, markdown } = parseMarkdownRule(content);
+    // Try to extract title from first heading if no name in frontmatter
+    let name = frontmatter.name;
+    if (!name) {
+        // Look for a heading in the markdown
+        const headingMatch = markdown.match(/^#\s+(.+)$/m);
+        if (headingMatch) {
+            name = headingMatch[1].trim();
+        }
+        else {
+            // Fall back to filename
+            name = basename(path).replace(/\.md$/, "");
+        }
+    }
+    return {
+        name,
+        rule: markdown,
+        globs: frontmatter.globs,
+        description: frontmatter.description,
+        alwaysApply: frontmatter.alwaysApply,
+        source: "rules-block",
+        ruleFile: path,
+    };

+
